questions.title: AI in different areas
questions.text: Give **one** example of using AI in the following areas.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Medicine (1): disease diagnosis; medical imaging interpretation; drug discovery and development; personalised treatment plans; robotic surgery; patient monitoring
Gaming industry (1): non-player characters / AI opponents; pathfinding; procedural generation of levels; dynamic difficulty; game testing; cheat detection
Industry (1): robots on assembly lines; predictive maintenance; quality control with computer vision; warehouse robots / logistics; demand forecasting
scheme.model_answer: Medicine: interpreting MRI scans to detect tumours. Gaming industry: controlling non-player characters that react to the player. Industry: predicting when machines will break down.

questions.title: Match the application to the area
questions.text: Match each AI application to the sphere where it is used.

left.text: Traffic lights that adapt to traffic in a smart city

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–Industry, L2–Education, L3–Medicine, L4–Gaming, L5–Society. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Predictive maintenance
questions.text: Describe how AI is used for **predictive maintenance** in a factory.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Sensors collect data from machines (vibration, temperature, noise) (1)
- AI learns the patterns that come before a failure and warns engineers to repair the machine before it breaks / schedules maintenance (1)

points.criterion: AI predicts failure so repairs are made in advance

scheme.model_answer: Sensors on each machine send data such as vibration and temperature to the AI, which recognises the patterns that appear before a breakdown and warns engineers to repair the machine before it fails.

questions.title: Quality control
questions.text: Explain how AI with **computer vision** improves quality control on a production line.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Cameras photograph every product and AI compares it with images of correct products / detects defects (1)
- faster / more consistent than human inspectors, works 24/7, faulty products are rejected automatically (1)

points.criterion: Benefit: faster / more consistent / every item checked

scheme.model_answer: Cameras photograph every item and the AI recognises defects such as cracks, so faulty items are removed automatically; it checks every product faster and more consistently than a human inspector.

questions.title: AI in industry
questions.text: Select **two** benefits of using AI-controlled robots in a factory.

options.content: They can work 24 hours a day
They can do dangerous tasks instead of workers

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.

questions.title: Adaptive learning
questions.text: Describe how an AI **adaptive learning** platform helps a student.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- It analyses the student's answers / performance (1)
- and chooses the next task at the right level / repeats weak topics / gives personalised feedback, so the student learns at their own pace (1)
scheme.model_answer: It analyses the student's previous answers and then gives tasks at the right level, repeating the topics the student finds difficult, so each student learns at their own pace.

questions.title: Risks of AI in education
questions.text: State **two** risks of using AI in education.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): over-reliance / students stop thinking for themselves; cheating with AI writing tools; incorrect or unfair automatic marking; privacy — student data collected; less human contact / no empathy; unequal access to devices
scheme.model_answer: 1 Students may use AI to write their essays instead of learning. 2 A lot of personal data about students is collected.

questions.title: Automatic marking
questions.text: AI marking systems can give students instant feedback on their answers.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.

questions.title: AI and medical images
questions.text: Describe how AI can be used to diagnose diseases from medical images.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any three (1 each):
- The AI (deep learning) is trained on many images (X-ray / MRI / CT) labelled by doctors
- It learns the patterns / features of a disease (e.g. tumour, fracture)
- A new scan is analysed and areas of concern are highlighted / a diagnosis is suggested
- It is fast / can be as accurate as specialists / a doctor checks the result

points.criterion: Analyses new scans and highlights / suggests diagnosis

scheme.model_answer: A deep-learning system is trained on thousands of X-ray images that doctors have labelled. It learns the patterns that show a disease such as pneumonia. When a new X-ray is analysed, it highlights suspicious areas and suggests a diagnosis, which a doctor then checks.

questions.title: Uses in medicine
questions.text: State **two** uses of AI in medicine **other than** diagnosing diseases from images.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): drug discovery; personalised treatment / dose; robot-assisted surgery; monitoring patients / wearables; predicting which patients will get worse; tracking epidemics; chatbots / appointment booking; speech-to-text medical notes
scheme.model_answer: 1 Discovering new medicines. 2 Smart watches that detect an irregular heartbeat.

questions.title: Responsibility in medicine
questions.text: Explain **one** ethical problem of using AI to make medical diagnoses.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Problem (1) + explanation (1), e.g.
- Accountability (1): if the AI gives a wrong diagnosis it is unclear whether the doctor, hospital or developer is responsible (1)
- Privacy (1): very sensitive patient data is needed to train / use it and could be leaked (1)
- Bias (1): trained on data from some groups, so less accurate for others (1)
- Black box (1): doctors / patients cannot see why it decided (1)
scheme.model_answer: If the AI gives a wrong diagnosis and the patient is harmed, it is unclear who is responsible — the doctor, the hospital or the company that made the AI.

questions.title: Non-player characters
questions.text: Describe how AI is used to control **non-player characters (NPCs)** in a computer game.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- AI decides the NPC's actions / behaviour (e.g. using behaviour trees / state machines / pathfinding) (1)
- so that NPCs react to the player's actions realistically, e.g. take cover, attack, work as a team, find a route around obstacles (1)

points.criterion: NPCs react to the player realistically (example)

scheme.model_answer: The AI decides what each enemy does, so it reacts to the player — for example it takes cover when shot at and uses pathfinding to move around walls — making the game more realistic.

questions.title: AI techniques in games
questions.text: Match each AI technique used in games to what it does.

right.text: Finds the shortest route for a character around obstacles
Creates new levels, maps and items automatically
Makes the game easier or harder depending on how well the player is doing
Lets an AI opponent improve by playing many games and receiving rewards

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Procedural generation
questions.text: Explain **one** benefit of procedural content generation for a game company.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Benefit (1) + explanation (1), e.g.
- Levels / worlds are created automatically (1) so fewer designers / less time and money are needed (1)
- Every game is different (1) so players keep playing longer / more replay value (1)
- Huge worlds can be produced (1) that would be impossible to design by hand (1)
scheme.model_answer: A new world is generated for every game, so players do not get bored and keep playing for longer.

questions.title: AI in society
questions.text: Complete the table with **one** example of how AI is used in each area of society.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Transport (1): self-driving cars; adaptive traffic lights; traffic prediction in navigation apps
Finance (1): fraud detection; credit scoring; banking chatbots; robo-advisers
Communication (1): voice assistants; machine translation; spam filters; predictive text
Environment (1): weather / climate prediction; monitoring deforestation / wildlife; crop disease detection; smart energy grids
scheme.model_answer: Transport: self-driving cars. Finance: detecting fraudulent card payments. Communication: machine translation. Environment: predicting the weather.
scheme.ai_instructions: Mark each row separately; the example must fit that area.

questions.title: Deepfakes
questions.text: Explain why **deepfakes** created with AI are a problem for society.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- AI can create realistic fake videos / audio of real people saying or doing things they never did (1)
- which can spread misinformation / damage reputations / be used for fraud or to influence elections; people stop trusting real media (1)

points.criterion: Realistic fake media of real people
Consequence: misinformation / fraud / loss of trust

scheme.model_answer: AI can make very realistic fake videos of real people saying things they never said, which can spread false information, damage someone's reputation or be used to cheat people out of money.

questions.title: Positive and negative effects
questions.text: State **one** positive effect and **one** negative effect of AI on society.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Positive (1): convenience / 24/7 services; safety (fewer accidents, fraud prevented); accessibility; new jobs / growth; help with climate / disease
Negative (1): unemployment; privacy / surveillance; bias; misinformation / deepfakes; accountability; dependence / loss of skills; security threats
scheme.model_answer: Positive: translation apps help people communicate in any language. Negative: routine jobs such as cashiers may disappear.

questions.title: AI in a rural hospital
questions.text:
A small hospital in a rural area has no radiologist. It plans to use an AI system to examine patients' X-rays and send the results to a doctor in the capital.

Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of this plan.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Benefits (max 2): patients get expert-level diagnosis without travelling; faster results / earlier treatment; works 24/7; the remote doctor only checks highlighted cases
Drawbacks (max 2): AI may make mistakes / miss rare conditions; unclear responsibility; sensitive data sent over the Internet — security / privacy; cost / needs reliable Internet; staff must trust and understand it
Balanced answer linked to the scenario for 4.

points.criterion: First benefit linked to the scenario

scheme.model_answer: Patients would get a quick diagnosis without travelling to the capital, so treatment can start earlier, and the AI can examine X-rays at any time of day. However, the AI might miss an unusual condition, and it is unclear who is responsible if it is wrong. Sending X-rays over the Internet also creates a risk that sensitive patient data is intercepted.
scheme.ai_instructions: Maximum 2 if only benefits or only drawbacks are given.

questions.title: A smart factory
questions.text: A car factory introduces AI robots on the assembly line, cameras that inspect each car, and an AI system that plans deliveries of parts.

parts.title: Cobots
parts.text: Some robots are **collaborative robots (cobots)**. Describe how AI allows them to work safely next to people.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Sensors / cameras detect people nearby and AI recognises them (1)
- the robot slows down / stops / changes its path to avoid hitting the worker (1)
scheme.model_answer: Cameras and sensors detect when a worker comes close, and the AI makes the robot slow down or stop so it does not hit the person.

parts.title: Planning deliveries
parts.text: Explain how AI can improve the planning of deliveries of parts.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- AI forecasts demand / how many parts will be needed from past production data (1)
- so parts arrive just in time — less stock stored, no shortages / best delivery routes save fuel (1)

points.criterion: Forecasts demand / plans routes from data
Benefit: no shortages / less stock / lower cost

scheme.model_answer: The AI predicts how many parts will be needed from production data, so suppliers deliver them just in time and the factory neither runs out of parts nor stores too many.

parts.title: Effect on workers
parts.text: Explain **one** effect of these changes on the factory's workers.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Effect (1) + explanation (1), e.g.
- Some workers lose their jobs (1) because robots do the routine assembly / inspection work (1)
- Workers need retraining (1) to maintain / program the robots (1)
- Safer work (1) because robots do the dangerous tasks (1)
scheme.model_answer: Some assembly workers may lose their jobs, because the robots now do the repetitive tasks they used to do.

questions.title: AI across spheres
questions.text: Describe how artificial intelligence is applied in **three** of the following spheres: industry, education, medicine, the gaming industry, society. For each sphere give a specific application and explain its benefit.

scheme.mark_scheme:
For each of three spheres: specific application described (1) + benefit explained (1).
Examples: industry — predictive maintenance prevents costly breakdowns; education — adaptive learning lets students learn at their own pace; medicine — image diagnosis finds disease earlier; gaming — NPC behaviour makes games realistic; society — fraud detection protects bank customers.
scheme.model_answer: In industry, AI analyses sensor data from machines to predict breakdowns, so engineers can repair them before they fail and production is not stopped. In medicine, deep-learning systems examine X-rays and MRI scans to detect diseases such as cancer, so patients are diagnosed earlier and treated sooner. In the gaming industry, AI controls non-player characters that react to the player's actions, which makes games more realistic and challenging.
scheme.ai_instructions: Mark the best three spheres. Vague applications such as 'AI is used in hospitals' do not score.

questions.text: Artificial intelligence is applied in many spheres.

parts.title: Examples

scheme.mark_scheme:

parts.title: Medical images
parts.text: Describe how AI is used to interpret medical images.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): trained on many labelled scans; learns patterns of diseases; analyses new scans and highlights abnormal areas / suggests a diagnosis; a doctor confirms
scheme.model_answer: The AI is trained on thousands of labelled scans, learns what diseased tissue looks like, and then highlights suspicious areas on new scans for a doctor to check.

parts.title: Risk in medicine
parts.text: Explain **one** risk of using AI in medicine.

scheme.mark_scheme: Risk (1) + explanation (1): wrong diagnosis harms patient / unclear responsibility; privacy of sensitive data; bias against some groups; black box — decisions cannot be explained; over-reliance by doctors
scheme.model_answer: AI systems need a lot of sensitive patient data, so if the data is hacked, patients' private medical information could be made public.

parts.title: Industry example
parts.text: State **one** use of AI in industry.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any one (1): assembly-line robots; predictive maintenance; quality control with computer vision; warehouse robots; demand forecasting; generative design
scheme.model_answer: Predictive maintenance of machines.

questions.title: A food-processing factory
questions.text: A food-processing factory in Kostanay plans to introduce AI to monitor its machines and to check the quality of its products.

parts.title: Predictive maintenance
parts.text: Describe how AI could be used to monitor the machines.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Sensors collect data (temperature, vibration) from the machines (1)
- AI recognises patterns that come before failure and warns engineers / schedules maintenance before a breakdown (1)
scheme.model_answer: Sensors send vibration and temperature data to the AI, which recognises the signs of a coming breakdown and warns engineers to repair the machine in time.

parts.title: Quality checks
parts.text: Explain how AI could check the quality of the products.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Cameras photograph each product and computer vision / AI detects defects (wrong shape, colour, damaged packaging) (1)
- faulty products are rejected automatically; every item is checked faster / more consistently than by people (1)
scheme.model_answer: Cameras photograph every packet and the AI spots damaged or badly sealed ones, which are removed automatically, so every item is checked quickly and consistently.

parts.title: Impact on the factory
parts.text: Discuss the impact of introducing AI on the factory and its workers.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Positive (max 2): fewer breakdowns / less downtime; higher quality / less waste; 24/7 production; safer work; new skilled jobs
Negative (max 2): job losses for inspectors / operators; retraining needed; high cost of AI and sensors; cyber-attack / system failure risk
Balanced answer for 4.

However, human quality inspectors might lose their jobs, and the remaining workers would need retraining to work with the AI. The system is also expensive to install.

questions.title: Games and society
questions.text: A games company in Almaty is developing an open-world adventure game. AI is also becoming common in everyday life outside games.

parts.title: Society

Negative effect (1) + explanation (1), e.g. job losses in routine work; surveillance reduces privacy; deepfakes spread misinformation; biased decisions

summary: How artificial intelligence is applied in industry, education, medicine, the gaming industry and society — what AI does in each sphere, real examples, benefits and risks.

theory.title: AI and where it is applied

blocks.content: The ability of computer systems to perform tasks that normally require **human intelligence**: perceiving (seeing, hearing), understanding language, reasoning, **learning from data**, planning and making decisions.

AI is used wherever there is **a lot of data**, a task that must be done **quickly, accurately or repeatedly**, or a job that is **dangerous** for people. To describe an application in the exam, say **what the AI does**, **how** (what data or technique), and **why it helps**.

blocks.title: Main AI capabilities used in applications
rows: Recognising objects, faces and defects in images and video
Detecting a tumour on an MRI scan
Finding patterns in past data to predict the future
Predicting when a machine will break down
Choosing the best action to reach a goal
Controlling machines that sense and act in the physical world
Suggesting items a user is likely to want

blocks.caption: The five spheres in this topic

items.title: Robotics and automation
items.content: **Industrial robots** with AI vision weld, paint, assemble and pack products on production lines. **Collaborative robots (cobots)** work safely next to people, slowing down when a worker comes close.

items.title: Predictive maintenance
items.content: Sensors on machines send data (vibration, temperature, noise). AI learns the patterns that come **before a breakdown** and warns engineers to repair the machine **before it fails** — avoiding expensive stoppages.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Cameras and **computer vision** inspect every product (bottles, chips, car parts) and reject faulty ones faster and more reliably than human inspectors.

items.title: Logistics and supply chain
items.content: AI **forecasts demand**, plans stock levels and delivery routes; robots in **warehouses** pick and move goods (e.g. Amazon). Self-driving trucks and drones deliver goods.

items.title: Energy and resources
items.content: AI controls heating, lighting and machines to **reduce energy use**; in mining and oil it analyses geological data to find deposits.

items.title: Design
items.content: **Generative design** — AI proposes thousands of shapes for a part that is strong but light; engineers choose the best.

blocks.title: AI in industry — benefits and risks
rows: **Job losses** for manual and routine workers
High **cost** of robots and AI systems

items.title: Adaptive (personalised) learning
items.content: The platform analyses each student's answers and chooses the **next task at the right level**, repeating topics the student finds hard (e.g. Duolingo, Khan Academy, this exam-prep platform's AI marking).

items.title: Intelligent tutoring systems and chatbots
items.content: AI tutors **explain**, give **hints** and answer students' questions at any time; chatbots answer common questions from students and parents.

items.title: Automatic marking and feedback
items.content: AI marks tests, essays and code and gives **instant feedback**, saving teachers' time.

items.title: Learning analytics
items.content: AI finds students who are **falling behind** or may drop out, so teachers can help early.

items.title: Accessibility
items.content: Speech-to-text, text-to-speech, automatic **subtitles** and **translation** help students with disabilities or a different home language.

items.title: Academic integrity
items.content: AI tools detect **plagiarism** and copied code; exam proctoring software monitors online exams.

blocks.title: AI in education — benefits and risks
rows: Learning at the student's **own pace** and level
Students may **over-rely** on AI and not think for themselves; cheating with AI writing tools
AI marking may be **wrong** or unfair for unusual answers
Teachers save time on marking and admin
**Privacy** — large amounts of student data are collected
Less **human contact**; AI cannot replace a teacher's empathy and motivation

items.title: Diagnosis and medical imaging
items.content: Deep-learning systems analyse **X-rays, CT/MRI scans, skin photos and eye scans** to detect cancer, fractures, pneumonia or diabetic eye disease — often as accurately as specialists and much faster.

items.title: Drug discovery
items.content: AI predicts how molecules will behave and which could become **new medicines**, reducing years of laboratory work (e.g. predicting protein structures with AlphaFold).

items.title: Personalised treatment
items.content: AI combines a patient's **medical history, genetics and test results** to suggest the most effective treatment and dose.

items.title: Robot-assisted surgery
items.content: Surgeons control robotic arms that make **precise, steady** movements through small cuts; AI can guide and stabilise the instruments.

items.title: Monitoring and prediction
items.content: **Wearables** (smart watches) track heart rate and detect irregular rhythms; hospital AI predicts which patients are at risk of getting worse; AI tracks the spread of **epidemics**.

items.title: Administration and virtual assistants
items.content: Chatbots book appointments and check symptoms; NLP converts doctors' speech into medical notes.

blocks.title: AI in medicine — benefits and risks
rows: A wrong diagnosis may harm the patient — **who is responsible**?
Very **sensitive personal data** — privacy and security
Bias if trained on data from only some groups of patients
Doctors spend less time on paperwork
Patients may not trust a "black box"; loss of human care

items.title: Non-player characters (NPCs)
items.content: AI controls the behaviour of enemies, allies and crowds: they **react to the player**, take cover, work as a team and make decisions (often with **finite-state machines** or **behaviour trees**).

items.title: Pathfinding
items.content: Algorithms such as **A\*** find the shortest route for characters around obstacles on the game map.

items.title: Procedural content generation
items.content: AI **generates levels, maps, landscapes, quests and items** automatically, so every game is different (e.g. Minecraft worlds, No Man's Sky planets).

items.title: Dynamic difficulty adjustment
items.content: The game watches how well the player is doing and makes it **easier or harder** to keep it challenging but fair.

items.title: AI opponents that learn
items.content: Programs such as **AlphaGo** and chess engines learned by **reinforcement learning** to beat world champions; similar AI plays strategy games.

items.title: Development and testing
items.content: AI bots **play-test** games to find bugs; AI generates graphics, animations and voices; **upscaling** (e.g. DLSS) makes graphics sharper at higher speed; AI detects **cheating** players.

blocks.title: AI in gaming — benefits and risks
rows: Very **addictive** personalised games and in-game purchases
Generated content may be repetitive or of low quality; artists' jobs

blocks.title: AI in everyday life
rows: Self-driving cars and buses; traffic-light control; navigation apps that predict traffic jams
Smart thermostats and lighting; energy grids that balance supply and demand; waste collection routes
Voice assistants; machine translation; spam filters; predictive text
Fraud detection on card payments; credit scoring; robo-advisers; banking chatbots
Face recognition; detecting cyber-attacks; predicting crime hot spots
Recommended posts, videos and music; content moderation; detecting fake news (and creating **deepfakes**)
Weather and climate prediction; drones detecting crop disease; monitoring deforestation and wildlife
Chatbots for government services; predicting demand for hospitals and schools

items.title: Positive effects on society
items.content:
- **Convenience** — services available 24/7, faster and personalised.
- **Safety** — fewer road accidents, fraud prevented, disasters predicted.
- **Accessibility** — translation, speech and image description help people with disabilities.
- **Economic growth** and new kinds of jobs (data scientists, AI engineers, ethicists).
- Help with global problems: climate, disease, food production.

items.title: Negative effects and ethical issues
items.content:
- **Unemployment** in routine jobs; growing **inequality**.
- **Privacy** and **mass surveillance**.
- **Bias and discrimination** in automated decisions.
- **Misinformation** — deepfakes and fake news; **filter bubbles** on social media.
- **Accountability** — who is responsible for an AI's harmful decision?
- **Security** — AI used for cyber-attacks or autonomous weapons.
- **Dependence** on AI and loss of human skills.

blocks.title: Using AI responsibly
blocks.content: Many countries are writing laws and guidelines for AI: decisions should be **transparent and explainable**, systems should be **tested for bias**, personal data must be **protected**, and a **human** should stay responsible for important decisions (medicine, justice, hiring).

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Give one example of using AI in the following areas. [3]**
*Medicine:* disease diagnosis from medical images / drug discovery / personalised treatment plans (1).
*Gaming industry:* non-player characters that react to the player / procedural generation of levels / dynamic difficulty (1).
*Education:* adaptive learning that adjusts tasks to each student / automatic marking (1).

**Q: Describe how AI is used for predictive maintenance in industry. [2]**
Sensors collect data such as **vibration and temperature** from machines (1); AI learns the patterns that come **before a failure** and warns engineers so the machine is **repaired before it breaks** (1).

**Q: Describe one way AI is used in the gaming industry. [2]**
AI controls **non-player characters** (1) so that they **react to the player's actions**, e.g. enemies take cover or attack as a team, making the game more realistic (1).

**Q: Explain one negative impact of AI on society. [2]**
AI can **automate routine jobs** such as cashiers and drivers (1), so many people may become **unemployed** and need retraining (1).

- Naming an area with **no specific application**: "AI is used in medicine" — say **what it does** (e.g. *detects tumours on scans*).
- Giving a benefit without saying **why** it helps (faster → earlier treatment).
- Describing a **robot** that only repeats fixed movements as AI — AI is needed when it **senses, decides or learns**.
- Repeating the same example for two areas.
